[Sir](../persons.html#939),
[Mr Furnival](../persons.html#531) has forwarded to me your proposal of dealing with me for my tale of the [Clever Woman of the Family](../books.html#58) as a book - I should be obliged if you would let me know your terms for publishing on commission; and like wise if in case of such an arrangement being practicable, whether you would take charge of my works that have been hitherto in [Mr Parker](../persons.html#1144)’s hands - All have been published by commission, excepting the two first, the [Heir of Redclyffe](../books.html#15) and [Heartsease](../books.html#19) which were on the half profit system, and respecting which it would be necessary to make an arrangement with Mr Parker -
The last years half profits on the Heir of Redclyffe were £28 .. 15 - on Heartsease £9..13 -
I mention this to facilitate your estimate of the worth of the half profits in case you should wish to purchase them
Your obt servt
C. M.

Yonge

[^1]: Black-edged paper.

[^2]: Serialised in Churchman\'s Family Magazine, Jan 1864 to March 1865 and published by Macmillan and Co. 1865.
